title: Group the ones (circular)
statement: A circular binary array. In one swap you exchange the values at any two positions. Return the minimum swaps to make all the 1s contiguous (around the circle).

solution.explanation: If there are k ones, the final block is some window of length k; the swaps needed equal the zeros inside it (each swap brings one 1 in). So find the length-k window (circularly: index mod n, or double the array) with the most ones. Fixed-size sliding window, Part 1.4.
solution.python:
def min_swaps(nums):
    k = sum(nums); n = len(nums)
    if k == 0: return 0
    cur = sum(nums[:k]); best = cur
    for i in range(k, n + k):
        cur += nums[i % n] - nums[(i - k) % n]; best = max(best, cur)
    return k - best
